review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the definitions of operatorNorm, choiLam and wedgeCoordinates and the whole of OperatorEntries.lean. I grepped the HyperbolicCones directory for existing zero or self lemmas for wedgeCoordinates and choiLam, and for uses of operatorNorm_eq_norm. I found no existing simp lemma for wedgeCoordinates v v or choiLam 0 y. I did not look at all 38 files that mention operatorNorm, so the downstream effect of the proposed @[simp] on operatorNorm_eq_norm is not checked. In particular, I did not check other files that use operatorNorm outside HyperbolicCones, which may be affected. I did not run Lean, so nothing here has been compiled or observed to loop.

findings.excerpt: have hz : wedgeCoordinates v v = 0 := by ext i; simp [wedgeCoordinates]
findings.problem: The degenerate cases wedgeCoordinates v v = 0 and choiLam 0 y = 0 are not available as lemmas. Both are proved in the proof body, and each proof unfolds the definition inside `simp [...]`. `choiLam` is a long expression with sums, so a plain `simp` cannot see that it vanishes at 0. Callers cannot use `simp` for `choiLam (wedgeCoordinates v v) y`; they must repeat the unfolding. A grep found no existing simp lemma for either fact.
findings.proposed_change: In Model.lean, next to the definitions, add `@[simp] theorem wedgeCoordinates_self (v : Vec 4) : wedgeCoordinates v v = 0` and `@[simp] theorem choiLam_zero_left (y : Fin 3 → R) : choiLam 0 y = 0`. Both have a definition-free LHS head, the RHS is strictly simpler, and neither rule can loop. The `hz`/`hc` steps in same_direction_zero then reduce to `simp` or `rw [wedgeCoordinates_self, choiLam_zero_left] at h`.
findings.benefit: The zero case is stated once and found automatically by `simp`. Downstream proofs about same-direction vectors no longer unfold `choiLam` or `wedgeCoordinates`. The normal form of `choiLam (wedgeCoordinates v v) y` becomes 0.

findings.problem: `operatorNorm_eq_norm : operatorNorm A = ‖A‖ := rfl` is not a simp lemma, so every consumer has to name it by hand. In HyperbolicCones it is passed explicitly to `simpa only`/`simp only`/`rw` in NormIdentity (lines 65 and 74), TangentIdentity (36 and 44), TangentRigidity (44) and OperatorEntries (17 and 21). `operatorNorm` is a reducible-looking wrapper around the norm, so the library's `norm_*` lemmas (`norm_smul`, `norm_zero`, `norm_nonneg`) do not fire on it by default. Without the rule, `simp` leaves `operatorNorm` terms in goals, and the lemmas operatorNorm_smul and operatorNorm_continuous are needed only to work around this.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `operatorNorm_eq_norm` as `@[simp]` in OperatorEntries.lean, so the canonical form is `‖A‖` with the L2-operator norm. Then the `simpa only [operatorNorm_eq_norm]`/`rw [..., operatorNorm_eq_norm]` calls can use plain `simpa`/`simp`. `operatorNorm_smul` would then be subsumed by `norm_smul` and should not also be tagged simp. This orientation (wrapper to norm) cannot cycle. Before committing, check other users of `operatorNorm` outside this directory.
findings.benefit: It removes the repeated manual rewrite, and the `norm_zero`/`norm_smul` simp lemmas apply to operator norms automatically. It also avoids two competing normal forms (`operatorNorm A` and `‖A‖`) in the same goals.
